result.reason: The operative language is acceptable at least as a customer-favorable variant of the fallback: Sparkling may assign to affiliates and M&A successors without consent, other assignments require consent not unreasonably withheld or delayed, Garman has no equivalent consent-free assignment right, and Sparkling's change of control creates no termination right. It does not achieve the preferred position because it lacks an express absolute prohibition on assignment by Garman to a Sparkling competitor. More importantly, the amendment to subsection (c) is overbroad: the reference to Section 20(d) could permit transfer, lease, export, or sublicensing of the Work merely because an assignment is permitted, thereby changing unrelated use and IP restrictions. The cross-reference should apply only to assignment of the Agreement. The added suspension and repricing language is also beyond the stated requirement, though commercially consistent with it.
